newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends unchanged at 35.75/76 vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends unchanged at 35.75/76 vs dollar.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed almost unchanged at 35.747/757 against the dollar in the spot market on Friday but slipped against the forward dollar, dealers said.
"It was very dull throughout," a dealer said.
Most of the day's deals were at 35.75 level.
Friday's major market moving news was that Indian Oil Corp was going for a syndicated loan to raise $1.0 billion to fund oil imports during 1997/98 (April-March), dealers said.
"The upshot is that they will be less dependent on dollar purchases from the market," a dealer said.
Bankers said part of the money from the loan would go to repay earlier loans which matured in April.
Despite the IOC news, spot rupee held fast to the 35.75 level, with some dealers reporting stray deals at 35.7450.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was absent for most of the day, but purchased very small amounts of dollars from the spot market just as the market was about to close, a dealer said.

The forward dollar premiums edged up in the morning session on the back of rising call money rates, softened as the day progressed and spurted towards the close again after the government announced a 30 billion bond issue on May 9.
The six month annualised forward premium closed at 4.65 percent compared to the previous close of 4.31 percent.
